items.followUp: What is a group in the periodic table? Give one example.

rubric.why: Elements in a family belong to the same group and have similar chemical properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that elements in the same group form a family and have similar chemical properties.

rubric.why: A suitable example identifies elements belonging to the same family.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving a correct example of a family.

modelAnswer: Elements in the same vertical group of the periodic table are called a family because they have similar chemical properties.
For example, lithium, sodium and potassium belong to Group 1 and are called the alkali-metal family.

items.followUp: What determines whether an element belongs to the s-block or p-block?

rubric.why: An element's block is determined by the subshell into which its last electron enters.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the block depends on the subshell receiving the last or differentiating electron.

rubric.why: The periodic table is divided into four blocks named s, p, d and f.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming all four blocks.

modelAnswer: A block is a set of elements in which the last electron enters the same type of subshell.
The periodic table has s, p, d and f blocks.

items.followUp: Define a single covalent bond and give one example.

rubric.why: A double covalent bond is formed by sharing two pairs of electrons between atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that two pairs of electrons are shared between two atoms.

rubric.why: The example must contain a double covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example, such as the oxygen molecule or a carbon–oxygen double bond.

modelAnswer: A double covalent bond is formed when two atoms share two pairs of electrons.
For example, the oxygen molecule has a double bond: O=O.

items.followUp: Why is the third ionization energy of magnesium much higher than its second ionization energy?

rubric.why: After the first ionization, Mg⁺ has configuration [Ne]3s¹, and the second electron is removed from this ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that the second electron is removed from Mg⁺, which has one electron in its 3s subshell.

rubric.why: The remaining electron is more strongly attracted in the positively charged ion, so removing it requires more energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the electron in Mg⁺ experiences greater attraction and therefore requires more energy to remove.

modelAnswer: Magnesium has the electron configuration [Ne]3s²; after the first ionization, Mg⁺ has the configuration [Ne]3s¹.
The second electron is removed from the positively charged Mg⁺ ion, where it experiences greater attraction, so more energy is required than for the first ionization.
